```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
invisible(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", "C.UTF-8"))
library(data.table)
library(DT)
A <- "docs/assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10"
st <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_stats.tsv"))
pts <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_points.tsv"))
fun <- fread(file.path(A, "fig3e_style_funnel.tsv"))
PAPER <- "Paper's cutoff"; BEFORE <- "Before FDR"; AFTER <- "After FDR"
SET_ORDER <- c(PAPER, BEFORE, AFTER)
tpl <- function(x) sub("hr", " hr", x)
hn <- pts[set == BEFORE & tp == "6hr" & gene == "HNRNPK" & variant_qual == "chr9:83980154:C>T"]
```

This page repeats the [comparison with GTEx Cerebellum sQTLs](isolaser_gtex_comparison.html)
for the [genotype-panel rerun](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html) of our permutation
test. In that rerun, a donor is used only if our genotype panel calls it
heterozygous, and associations come from every recorded variant × exonic part.
The original page and its results are unchanged.

As before, we compare our allelic splicing effects (isoLASER ΔPSI) with GTEx v8
Cerebellum sQTL effects (beta), as in the right panel of
[Fig. 3e of the isoLASER paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-64605-6).
We use each event's **skipping junction**, whose usage falls when the exonic
part is included, so a **negative correlation** is expected.

# How pairs were matched

The matching is unchanged:

- **Variant and gene:** the same SNV (position, REF and ALT; isoLASER's
  0-based position + 1 = GTEx's) tested for the same Ensembl gene in GTEx.
- **GTEx data:** full Cerebellum summary statistics, every tested association
  at any p-value.
- **Event:** the exonic part must form an annotated exon-skipping or
  alternative-splice-site event, and the GTEx junction must be exactly that
  event's skipping junction.
- **Points:** each point is one **pair**: an isoLASER association (variant ×
  exonic part) and its matched GTEx skipping junction, at one timepoint.

Our associations come in three sets:

- **Paper's cutoff:** isoLASER's own `cis` label and pooled ΔPSI, as in the
  paper. This set doesn't depend on our donor rule, so it is the same as on the
  original page.
- **Before FDR:** the rerun's screen. The donors are panel-heterozygous with
  ≥ 10 reads, with ≥ 20 reads over those donors, `cis`, |ΔPSI| ≥ 0.10, part
  ≥ 10 bp, and no other candidate variant within 30 bp.
- **After FDR:** the rerun's screen plus permutation BH q < 0.05 within each
  timepoint, as on the [rerun's FDR page](isolaser_fdr_panel10.html).

**Example, HNRNPK.** The C>T variant (chr9:83980154, 0-based) and the 34-base
exonic part (gold) form an alternative splice site. GTEx measures the
skipping junction (blue), which jumps over the part. At 6 hours, ALT changes
part inclusion by `r sprintf("%+.1f", 100*hn$dpsi)` percentage points in the
rerun. GTEx's beta for the skipping junction is `r sprintf("%+.2f", hn$slope)`:
opposite signs, as expected.

![](assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/comparable_event_example_skipping.png)

```{r funnel}
f <- fun[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
             `Our associations (SNVs)`=reported_snv_associations, `Same variant and gene tested in GTEx`=tested_in_gtex,
             `Plotted pairs`=plotted, Genes=genes)]
knitr::kable(f, align="llrrrr")
```

**Our associations (SNVs)**: variant × exonic part associations with a
single-base variant at that timepoint. **Same variant and gene tested in
GTEx**: of those, the ones whose variant GTEx Cerebellum tests for the same
gene. **Plotted pairs**: association × matched GTEx skipping junction.

Every SNV in the rerun is in our genotype panel, so far more of our
associations are tested in GTEx. Before FDR,
`r paste(range(round(100 * fun[set == BEFORE, tested_in_gtex / reported_snv_associations])), collapse="–")`%
are tested, against 40–55% on the original page. After FDR it is
`r paste(range(round(100 * fun[set == AFTER, tested_in_gtex / reported_snv_associations])), collapse="–")`%,
against 13–30%. In the original run's before-FDR set, 92% of the associations
GTEx doesn't test used a variant absent from our panel, against 5% of those it
does test.

# Result

![](assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/fig3e_style.png)

[Download PDF](assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/fig3e_style.pdf)

```{r stats}
s <- dcast(st[subset %in% c("all", "GTEx p < 1e-5")], set + tp ~ subset, value.var=c("n", "expected_sign", "pearson_r", "pearson_p"))
s <- s[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp),
           `Pairs`=n_all, `All: R (p)`=fifelse(is.na(pearson_r_all), "too few",
             sprintf("%.2f (%s)", pearson_r_all, vapply(pearson_p_all, function(x) format(signif(x, 2)), ""))),
           `All: expected sign`=sprintf("%d/%d", expected_sign_all, n_all),
           `GTEx p < 1e-5: expected sign`=fifelse(is.na(`n_GTEx p < 1e-5`), "none", sprintf("%d/%d", `expected_sign_GTEx p < 1e-5`, `n_GTEx p < 1e-5`)))]
knitr::kable(s, align="llrrrr")
```

**R (p)**: Pearson correlation of our ΔPSI with GTEx's beta, with its p-value.
A negative R is expected. **Expected sign**: pairs where our ΔPSI and GTEx's
beta have opposite signs. **GTEx p < 1e-5**: only pairs where GTEx itself has
strong evidence.

## Direction where GTEx is significant

As on the original page, we take pairs where GTEx is significant (nominal
p < 0.05, the blue points). A pair is **consistent** when our ΔPSI and GTEx's
beta have opposite signs. A binomial test asks whether the share of consistent
pairs differs from 50%. Here we use the rerun's two sets; the paper's-cutoff
set is the same as on the original page. These definitions are our own; the
paper reports only the correlation.

```{r consistency}
bt <- function(d) {
  k <- sum(d$dpsi * d$slope < 0); n <- nrow(d)
  data.table(Pairs=n, Consistent=k, `Consistent (%)`=if (n) round(100 * k / n) else NA_real_,
             `Binomial p, two-sided`=if (n) signif(binom.test(k, n)$p.value, 2) else NA_real_,
             `Binomial p, one-sided`=if (n) signif(binom.test(k, n, alternative="greater")$p.value, 2) else NA_real_)
}
cons <- rbindlist(lapply(c(BEFORE, AFTER), function(x) {
  blue <- pts[set == x & pval_nominal < 0.05 & dpsi != 0]
  once <- blue[, .(dpsi=mean(dpsi), slope=slope[1]), by=.(Gene_name, variant_qual, exonic_part, phenotype_id)]
  rbind(blue[order(tp), bt(.SD), by=.(Timepoint=tpl(tp))],
        data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, every point", bt(blue)),
        data.table(Timepoint="All timepoints, each pair once", bt(once)))[, Set := x]
}))
knitr::kable(cons[, c("Set", setdiff(names(cons), "Set")), with=FALSE], align="llrrrrr")
```

**Pairs**: association × GTEx skipping junction with GTEx p < 0.05.
**Consistent**: pairs with opposite signs. **Two-sided p**: is the share
different from 50%. **One-sided p**: is it above 50%, the direction expected.
**Every point** counts each timepoint's points, so a pair called at several
timepoints counts several times. **Each pair once** uses each pair's mean ΔPSI
over the timepoints where it is called.

# Data

```{r points}
d <- pts[order(match(set, SET_ORDER), tp, gene), .(Set=set, Timepoint=tpl(tp), Gene=gene,
  Variant=variant_qual, `Exonic part`=exonic_part, `GTEx junction`=paste0(intron_start_0, "-", intron_end_0),
  `Our dPSI`=round(dpsi, 3), `Our BH q`=signif(q_bh, 2), `GTEx beta`=signif(slope, 3), `GTEx p`=signif(pval_nominal, 2))]
DT::datatable(as.data.frame(d), rownames=FALSE, filter="top", options=list(pageLength=10, scrollX=TRUE))
```

**Variant**: isoLASER's 0-based position. **GTEx junction**: 0-based,
half-open intron coordinates. **Our BH q** is blank for the paper's-cutoff set,
which has no permutation test. Download the
[points](assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/fig3e_style_points.tsv) and
[statistics](assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/fig3e_style_stats.tsv).

Reproduce from `long_read_RNA/10.isolaser_permutation/` with
`ADAPTIVE_RULE=panel10`:
1. `python 27.gtex_fdr_comparison.py --prepare-full-cerebellum`, then the same with `--before-fdr`;
2. `Rscript 34.extract_full_cerebellum.R`, then the same with `--before-fdr`;
3. `Rscript 36.plot_fig3e_style.R` and `Rscript 29.gtex_comparable_examples.R --skipping`.

With that setting, everything is written under `out/adaptive_panel10/` and
`docs/assets/isolaser_gtex_panel10/`. The paper's-cutoff set is read from the
original run without being changed.
